narrative:
The differentially abundant metabolites strongly point to **Eicosanoid synthesis** (Wikipathways WP167; FDR≈0, fold enrichment ≈1001) as the dominant affected pathway. Five input compounds map to this pathway: arachidonic acid (C00219), leukotriene A4 (C00909), 15-HETE (C04742), 5-HETE (C04805), and 15-deoxy-Δ¹²,¹⁴-PGJ₂ (C14717). A secondary, selenium micronutrient network (WP15) also achieves a significant FDR, but the eicosanoid cluster is the tighter and more biologically interpretable signal.

**Driver compounds and upstream/downstream relationships.** Arachidonic acid (C00219) is the canonical substrate for this pathway, confirmed as a member of KEGG Arachidonic Acid Metabolism (map00590). KEGG reaction graph traversal confirms that arachidonic acid is directly upstream of leukotriene A4 (C00909) via a two-hop route (arachidonic acid → C05356 → leukotriene A4), establishing a directional substrate-to-product relationship. The HETEs (5-HETE and 15-HETE) are downstream lipoxygenase products of arachidonic acid, and the PGJ₂ derivative is a cyclopentenone prostaglandin downstream branch. Gentisic acid (C00628) and dihydrothymine (C00906) are not eicosanoid pathway members and may reflect parallel oxidative-stress or pyrimidine-degradation signals.

**Biological significance.** Coordinated elevation of arachidonic acid alongside its lipoxygenase and cycloxygenase offspring suggests activation of the canonical inflammatory eicosanoid cascade in the treatment group. Elevated leukotriene A4 (the precursor to the potent chemotactic leukotriene B4) and 5-HETE are consistent with neutrophil recruitment and type-2 inflammatory signaling. The 15-HETE and 15-deoxy-PGJ₂ arms reflect lipoxygenase and cyclopentenone prostaglandin routes that modulate resolution and adaptive immunity. The copper (C00070) and hypochlorite (C19697) hits likely intersect with oxidative bursts and myeloperoxidase activity, reinforcing a broader inflammatory milieu. Histamine (C00388) further signals mast-cell or allergic-type inflammation superimposed on the eicosanoid-driven response.
